newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Orogen tops turnover list on debut.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Orogen tops turnover list on debut.

text.p: Shares in Orogen Minerals Ltd, which holds the resources assets of the Papua New Guinea government, topped the Australian share market's turnover list on Friday as investors took profits on the first day of trading.
Orogen shares listed on the Australian Stock Exchange at A$2.05 and reached a day's high of A$2.13.
Brokers said most of the sellers were Australiaa retail investors who acquired Orogen shares at A$1.70, giving them a profit of 25 percent based on the closing price of A$2.12.
"There was buying right across the board, but it was mostly from institutions who missed out on the offer," one broker said.
Orogen easily topped the turnover list with 13.10 million shares traded.

The float was based on an offering by the PNG government of a 49 percent in the Mineral Resources Development Corp, which owns strategic assets in key PNG gold projects such as Lihir, Porgera, and Misima, along with the Kutubu and Gobe oilfields.

Of the 153.69 million shares offered, half went to institutions at A$2.00 per share after an open-bid tender, with 20 percent to Australian residents and 30 percent to PNG residents and local institutions. The offer closed with applications from institutions for A$2.0 billion of shares.
Orogen's shareholders lists shows that 20 PNG and international institutions own 71.68 percent of the shares with the five largest owners all based in PNG.
One broker involved in the transactions said international currency investor and funds manager George Soros had taken shares in the float process.
PNG deputy prime minister and finance minister Chris Haiveta said at the Oregon listing ceremony that the PNG government would not interfere in the company's operations.
